name: Conceptual Physics Course Bank Profile
role: Course-specific layer after universal Philosophy and `_question_structure.zip`. Owns Physics I-can-first architecture, response mix, source/visual behavior, course-resolved counts, representation system, conceptual-before-computational sequencing, and Summative profile; does not redefine universal build/package mechanics.

instructional_spine.hard_rule: Exact Assessment Plan I-can statements are the atomic center of Bank design and downstream routing. Learning Targets group the I-cans; Mastery Goals organize/report accumulated evidence. Never build section quotas first and attach I-can labels afterward.
planning_sequence: Resolve exact I-can IDs/text from curriculum/i_can_index.json.
Build one evidence specification / mini-bank plan per I-can.

Using the dedicated `_question_structure.zip`, map content modes, formula/reverse paths, vocabulary directions, best-fit structures, representations/tools, and legitimate parallel variation for each I-can.
Build unitN_question_design_map.json before any final student prompt is authored.
Route the planned I-can mini-banks into Notes/Practice/CYU/Warm-Ups/Exit/Summative and reconcile destination totals.
Author questions from the plan, independently solve/verify them, then derive DOK/Bloom/final family metadata.
instructional_spine.disciplinary_practices: Use the Assessment Plan recurring-practice map as a menu for evidence design, not a quota.

inventory.notes_pair_rule: No more than four canonical Example/YTI pairs per section; use fewer only when the Assessment Plan/source genuinely does not support four meaningful anchors.
inventory.granularity: Counts are separate canonical questions/tasks; do not bundle unrelated jobs to satisfy counts.
inventory.allocation_rule: Inventory totals are destination containers only. NEVER compute I-can quotas by evenly dividing the container (for example 24/3=8). Build intentional I-can mini-banks first, then reconcile to the destination total.
inventory.notes_i_can_floor: Every exact section I-can receives at least one complete Example/YTI pair before any fourth/enrichment pair is allocated.
inventory.wtc_rule: Every WTC is one true connected multi-part FRQ-decomposition routine; normally 3-5 labeled parts. WTC content may be cross-Unit and is excluded from current-Unit I-can coverage.

abundance_philosophy.rule: Physics Practice may intentionally repeat a high-value conceptual or quantitative family with changed values, diagrams, contexts, or representations. Useful repetition is not a defect.
abundance_philosophy.teacher_choice: Teacher may skip items; keep a rich usable Bank rather than a minimum packet.
abundance_philosophy.anti_template_rule: Do not let one CER shell, one justify suffix, one graph type, or one Student A/Student B scaffold spread across unrelated targets.

response_mode.canonical_instructional: constructed/open response is the default; selected response is allowed only when the destination/purpose benefits from it and the current Base/Framework destination permits it
response_mode.distractors: item-specific misconceptions only; no generic Physics vocabulary distractor bag

representations.rule: Representations are evidence, not decoration. Inspect the Hewitt/source visual library before defaulting to text-only in representation-heavy sections.
representations.answer_neutrality: NEVER SHOW THE ANSWER IN THE STUDENT IMAGE. If students must identify/infer/rank/label/calculate/predict/critique/construct/determine something, remove that answer-bearing label/arrow/value/rank/highlight/path/conclusion from the student visual. Source and reusable figures are conditional references, not automatically student-safe.

conceptual_before_computational.rule: Establish the physical model/relationship qualitatively before formula substitution whenever the concept supports it. Quantitative work should end with physical interpretation when that is part of the mapped job.

question_structure.generic_toolkit: current `_question_structure.zip` = universal authoritative design/variation structures; Framework Hewitt/section libraries = Physics-specific enrichment only
question_structure.rule: Use `_question_structure.zip` first for universal structure choices. Then use Physics/Hewitt libraries as course-specific menus. Do not force every family into every section and do not let Framework libraries become a competing universal taxonomy.

source_hierarchy: Original Unit Assessment Plan = scope/evidence authority
Extracted Conceptual Physics/Hewitt = primary conceptual voice + captured visual-story source + question-family benchmark
Course-aligned Physics section packets/approved figures = strongest ready-to-use course reference
OpenStax High School Physics = secondary explanation/examples/representations

summative.v5_v6: genuine makeup/alternate forms, not reordered/numeric-only copies
summative.i_can_coverage: Every form V1-V6 directly samples every exact Unit I-can at least once; remaining items are intentionally weighted toward high-leverage/compound Mastery-Goal evidence.
summative.security_hard_rule: No exact prompt duplication within a form, across V1-V6, or against exposed instructional items. Parallel forms may assess the same I-can/family but must use genuinely independent evidence stimuli; V5/V6 require especially distinct contexts/representations/structures.

review_view.rule: Generate unitN_review.html from the same canonical items, grouped first by exact I-can then question_family_id. The I-can grouping is the primary side-by-side human comparison view.
review_view.card_metadata: Every card displays destination, exact i_can_id, colored audit_status, and the exact I-can statement.

resource_sequence_view.rule: Generate from the same canonical items as unitN.html. Use the normal stacked bank-item cards; do not use side-by-side review grids.

ordering.WTC: all Unit WTC items in section order
ordering.EX/YTI: section order; each Example immediately followed by its paired YTI; then next pair
ordering.Warm-Ups: section order, Warm-Up 1 through 3, preserving item order
ordering.Exit Tickets: section order, Exit A through C, preserving item order
ordering.Summative Assessments: V1 through V6, preserving question order

resource_sequence_view.note: This is a teacher audit/resource-sequence view, not a new source of canonical questions.

audit_status.display: Destination · I-can ID · colored status — exact I-can statement
audit_status.fresh_build_rule: All canonical items start NEEDS AUDIT even if mechanical/semantic builder QA passes.

wtc_frq.hard_rule: Every WTC is one coherent free-response-style shared stimulus with connected labeled parts, normally 3-5. It is authored to practice how students unpack and navigate a long question, not to prove current-section mastery.
wtc_frq.content_scope: May draw from any Unit in the current Physics course. Current-section/current-Unit alignment is optional.
wtc_frq.coverage_rule: WTC never satisfies the current Unit I-can coverage floors. Its i_can_id/i_can text is a content provenance address and may resolve to another Unit in curriculum/i_can_index.json.
wtc_frq.unfamiliar_content_rule: When content has not yet been taught, parts must remain accessible as unpacking, representation, qualitative prediction, relationship selection, or solution-planning practice rather than requiring successful execution of an untaught procedure.

canonical_fields.wtc_frq_focus: non-empty list of FRQ breakdown moves

wtc_frq.source_reference_rule: External/released/workbook FRQs may inform morphology only. Do not copy their wording, data, figures, or solution sequence into a Bank WTC.

question_design_map.universal_authority: bundled `_question_structure.zip` supplied by the Base Bank PM
question_design_map.hard_rule: No multi-item Physics Bank authoring begins from blank prompt generation. Map I-can evidence/question variety and representations first, instantiate item slots in JSON, then author from those slots.
question_design_map.no_quota: Question type/wording/representation variety is selected by I-can fit; there are no universal percentages.
question_design_map.dok_bloom: DOK/Bloom are never preplanned quotas; assign after the finished item exists.

destination_authoring_preferences.example_yti: When an I-can naturally supports mathematical/formula application, prefer strong contextual quantitative/formula Example/YTI anchors over generic conceptual or vocabulary filler. Preserve conceptual/model meaning; equations are relationships, not answer machines.
destination_authoring_preferences.practice: Plan a target-appropriate mix that may include matching, vocabulary in multiple directions, direct/inverse formula use, dependent multi-step, graphs/data, diagrams/FBDs/vectors, short conceptual response, misconception diagnosis, and transfer. No universal percentages.
destination_authoring_preferences.warmups: Keep the established retrieval/bridging pattern unless the Assessment Plan requires a specific change.
destination_authoring_preferences.exit_tickets: Within each four-question ticket and across A/B/C, vary evidence modes when the I-can supports it. Do not make four same-shell questions. Treat Exit Ticket as formative-secure for semantic-independence QA.
destination_authoring_preferences.wtc: Keep the normal Bank card/metadata/answer/alignment display. WTC content is FRQ morphology/decomposition practice and may be cross-Unit.

authoring_context_rule.hard_rule: Do not write naked plug-and-chug prompts that only assign variables and request a solve. Begin with a concrete physical situation/phenomenon that naturally supplies measurements; then students may choose/use/rearrange/interpret the relationship.
authoring_context_rule.equation_role: Equations are relationships describing the phenomenon, not answer machines.
